benchmark.category: a ride-hailing and on-demand delivery app for Indian cities — cab, bike, e-rickshaw, parcel and hourly rental
benchmark.users: customers booking rides and parcels from their phones, driver partners earning fares trip by trip, and a super admin running approvals, pricing and bookings

requirements.source_phrase: why you use py for backend i need node js for backend
requirements.statement: Every /api request is answered by the Node.js backend the app runs (the Node server process serves the route); with the Python server stopped every API route still responds identically, and any Python file left in the deployment only forwards requests and contains no route logic of its own
requirements.notes: The user's latest demand was Node.js and the answer choice was 'Rewrite the backend in Node.js'. app_summary says the backend is Python with MongoDB, which contradicts the user; files_of_reference lists /app/backend-node/server.js and describes /app/backend/server.py as a proxy only, so Phase 4 must confirm the served API comes from Node, not from the Python process.

requirements.source_phrase: but don't change any logic only change the backend language but don't change logic
requirements.statement: Every route the app exposes (auth, customer bookings, driver, admin, geo) answers on the same path with the same HTTP status, the same JSON field names and the same error shapes as before the rewrite — errors as an object with a detail string, validation failures as 422 with a detail entry per bad field — and no route answers 500 where the previous backend returned a defined 4xx
requirements.notes: The user's instruction was to change only the language. The inherited suite (R-003 to R-074) holds each individual behaviour; this requirement holds the shared contract of paths, status codes and response shapes, which a rewrite most easily breaks while each screen still looks fine.

requirements.source_phrase: i need full document that how can a super admin , driver , customer signup and all functionality
requirements.statement: Opening /docs/Safar_User_Guide.pdf from a shared link with no session shows or downloads a PDF whose text covers signup and the features for each role — customer (booking a cab, bike, e-rickshaw, parcel and hourly rental, live trip and OTP, cancelling, paying, rating, trip history), driver partner (signup, application and approval, online/offline, accepting, directions, arrival, OTP start, release, completing, earnings) and super admin (how the admin is created, dashboard, driver approval and suspension, all bookings, pricing, users and roles) — plus a reference section of statuses, fares and limits
requirements.notes: The user asked for a full document covering signup and all functionality for the three roles; the [Agent] reply reports an 11-page PDF with text and tables only, no screenshots. Coverage of each role's signup and features is the requirement; screenshots are not, so their absence is not a failure.

requirements.source_phrase: i need full document that how can a super admin , driver , customer signup and all functionality
requirements.statement: GET /docs/Safar_User_Guide.pdf without a session returns 200 with PDF content (Content-Type application/pdf) and the complete file with extractable text and tables, and the path is served as that file rather than being swallowed by the single-page-app history fallback and returning the HTML shell
requirements.notes: The [Agent] reply gives the document at a preview-domain URL; the file must ship in the deployment and sit outside the SPA fallback, which is the usual way a /docs asset turns into an HTML page that will not open as a PDF. Check the page count is stable and the text layer extracts.

requirements.statement: Against the Node backend, the seeded customer's home screen lists the five services, /book/cab shows fare options once a pickup and drop are set, and the seeded super admin's /admin/stats renders its counts, with no screen showing a network, server or JSON-parse error
requirements.notes: features_or_bugs_to_test requires 'Frontend still works end-to-end against the Node backend (quick smoke: customer home, booking screen shows fare options, admin overview)'. Derived from the build description, not from a [USER] line: the rewrite must not leave the screens pointing at response shapes the new backend no longer sends.

requirements.statement: A booking left in 'searching' for 30 minutes is moved once by the server to 'cancelled' with a non-empty cancellation reason even with no client request, it then stops appearing in /api/driver/requests and stops blocking that customer's next booking, while a booking already accepted, arrived or started at the 30-minute mark is left untouched
requirements.notes: app_summary: 'Bookings no driver accepts within 30 minutes are auto-cancelled with a reason shown.' The user required the rewrite to change no logic, so this fix must survive it; the inherited suite has no requirement for it. Testing needs clock control or a booking with its created time set back, and must confirm the job cannot run twice and write two reasons.

requirements.statement: POST /api/bookings/{id}/start with a wrong OTP returns 400 and reduces that booking's remaining attempts; after five wrong attempts a further attempt is refused with 429 and does not move the booking out of 'arrived', while a correct OTP within the first five attempts moves it to 'started'
requirements.notes: app_summary: the driver's OTP entry is 'limited to 5 attempts'. Inherited R-030 covers a single wrong OTP but not the limit. Check the counter is per booking, that a correct OTP at attempt five still works, and that a trip is never left unable to start without a release path.

requirements.statement: POST /api/bookings/{id}/release by the assigned driver puts the booking back to 'searching' with a fresh OTP, clears the driver assignment, makes it visible again in other matching online drivers' /api/driver/requests, and the previous OTP no longer starts the trip; a driver not assigned to the booking is refused and the booking is unchanged
requirements.notes: app_summary: 'A driver who can't make it can release the trip, and it goes back to other drivers.' The rewrite must preserve it and the inherited suite has no requirement for it. Verify the new OTP differs from the old and that the customer's screen shows a new searching state rather than a stale driver.

requirements.statement: A customer whose booking no driver accepted within 30 minutes sees it on /trip/:id as cancelled with the reason written in words on screen, and the home screen no longer offers it as the active booking and lets the customer book again
requirements.notes: The user-visible half of the auto-cancel fix: the reason must render, not an empty status or a spinner that never resolves.

requirements.statement: The assigned driver's trip screen offers a release control while the trip is accepted or arrived; operating it returns the driver to the requests list with that booking gone and shows a confirmation, and the control reports its result or the server's error on screen
requirements.notes: Control-exists check: the action must fire and the screen must change state; a refused release must leave the trip displayed and say why.

requirements.statement: A super admin suspending an approved driver from /admin/drivers persists the suspension, and the suspended driver can then no longer go online, see requests or accept one (the call is refused and no booking is assigned), while reinstating the driver restores online, requests and accept
requirements.notes: app_summary and features_or_bugs_to_test give the super admin driver approval and suspension; approval is inherited (R-038/R-046) but suspension is not covered. The refusal must be a clean 4xx with the driver's existing trips untouched.

requirements.statement: On a shared device, after one customer signs out and a second customer signs in, no screen shows the first customer's name, trip or booking list from cached state, and signing back in as the first customer shows only that customer's own trips
requirements.notes: The [Agent] reports this fix ('On a shared phone, the next person to sign in no longer sees the previous user's trips') and app_summary repeats it; the rewrite must not reintroduce a cached store. The server half is inherited R-052 (the previous token is rejected); here the assertion is that the screen renders no stale signed-in data.

requirements.statement: The facts the guide states about the product — that only cash payment is active while UPI and card are marked coming soon, that no ready-made super admin password exists and the admin email must be designated before signup, and the fare formula with its starting fare values — match the app's actual behaviour and the fare configuration returned by /api/services and /api/fare-estimate
requirements.notes: Files/generated-artifact class: the guide is a promise made to the user, and a guide that contradicts the app misleads the reader. Derived from the build description of the guide's reference section (statuses, starting fares, rules and limits, payments). Compare the stated values against the stored fare configuration rather than against a screenshot.

requirements.statement: GET /manifest.webmanifest returns 200 with JSON naming the app, a start_url, standalone display and at least one icon path that resolves to a real image, and the service worker script path returns JavaScript with 200 rather than the single-page-app index.html
requirements.notes: The [Agent] message tells the user to use Add to Home Screen on iPhone and Install app on Android, and app_summary calls the product 'installable to the home screen'. The history fallback commonly serves HTML for both paths, which silently kills installability.

requirements.statement: A phone browser opening the app is offered Add to Home Screen / Install, and once installed the app opens in standalone display at the start URL with every route (landing, sign-in, booking, trip, driver, admin) rendering without the browser chrome
requirements.notes: Product shell: the build tells the user the app installs to the home screen like a normal app, so this promise must hold in the deployed build, not only be present as files.
